content: Phenobarbital has significant interactions with various drugs, primarily by affecting their metabolism through hepatic and intestinal enzymes, particularly CYP3A4, CYP2C19, and CYP2C9/10. Below is a detailed explanation of these interactions: 1. Darolutamide: Phenobarbital increases the metabolism of darolutamide, reducing its levels and therapeutic effects. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 2. Darunavir: Phenobarbital decreases darunavir levels by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to therapeutic failure and resistance. Coadministration is contraindicated. 3. Dasatinib: Phenobarbital reduces dasatinib levels by increasing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Deferasirox: Phenobarbital decreases deferasirox levels. Avoid potent UGT inducers or increase the deferasirox dose to 30 mg/kg while monitoring ferritin levels and clinical response. 5. Deflazacort: Phenobarbital reduces deflazacort levels via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 6. Desipramine: Both phenobarbital and desipramine increase sedation. Monitor closely for additive sedative effects. 7. Dexamethasone: Phenobarbital reduces dexamethasone levels through CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Dexbrompheniramine and Dexchlorpheniramine: Both drugs increase sedation when combined with phenobarbital. Monitor closely. 9. Dexfenfluramine: Phenobarbital increases sedation, while dexfenfluramine decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution. 10. Dexlansoprazole: Phenobarbital reduces dexlansoprazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 11. Dexmedetomidine: Both drugs increase sedation. Monitor closely. 12. Dexmethylphenidate: Phenobarbital increases sedation, while dexmethylphenidate decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution. 13. Dextroamphetamine: Phenobarbital increases sedation, while dextroamphetamine decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution. 14. Dextromoramide and Diamorphine: Both drugs increase sedation when combined with phenobarbital. Monitor closely. 15. Diazepam: Phenobarbital reduces diazepam levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism, while both drugs increase sedation. Monitor closely. 16. Diclofenac: Phenobarbital reduces diclofenac levels by increasing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Monitor closely. 17. Dienogest/Estradiol Valerate: Phenobarbital reduces the efficacy of this contraceptive by increasing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. Avoid use for at least 28 days after discontinuing phenobarbital. 18. Diethylpropion: Phenobarbital increases sedation, while diethylpropion decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution. 19. Difelikefalin and Diphenoxylate HCl: Both drugs increase sedation when combined with phenobarbital. Monitor closely. 20. Digoxin: Phenobarbital reduces digoxin levels via P-glycoprotein efflux. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Dihydroergotamine: Phenobarbital reduces dihydroergotamine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 22. Diltiazem: Phenobarbital reduces diltiazem levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Dimenhydrinate: Both drugs increase sedation. Monitor closely. 24. Diphenhydramine: Both drugs increase sedation. Monitor closely. 25. Disopyramide: Phenobarbital reduces disopyramide levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 26. Dobutamine: Phenobarbital increases sedation, while dobutamine decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution. 27. Docetaxel: Phenobarbital reduces docetaxel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux. Monitor closely. 28. Dolutegravir: Phenobarbital increases dolutegravir metabolism, reducing its levels and efficacy. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 29. Donepezil: Phenobarbital reduces donepezil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 30. Dopamine: Phenobarbital increases sedation, while dopamine decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution. 31. Doravirine: Phenobarbital reduces doravirine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to virologic failure and resistance. Coadministration is contraindicated. 32. Dosulepin and Doxepin: Both drugs increase sedation when combined with phenobarbital. Monitor closely. 33. Doxorubicin: Phenobarbital reduces doxorubicin levels by increasing elimination. Monitor closely. 34. Doxycycline: Phenobarbital reduces doxycycline levels by increasing metabolism. Monitor closely. 35. Dronabinol: Phenobarbital reduces dronabinol levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Monitor closely. 36. Dronedarone: Phenobarbital reduces dronedarone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 37. Dropperidol: Both drugs increase sedation. Monitor closely. 38. Dulaglutide: Phenobarbital may affect the absorption of dulaglutide due to its impact on gastric emptying. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Duloxetine: Phenobarbital reduces duloxetine levels via CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 40. Dupilumab: Dupilumab may normalize CYP450 enzyme activity, potentially altering phenobarbital metabolism. Monitor closely. 41. Dutasteride: Phenobarbital reduces dutasteride levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 42. Duvelisib: Phenobarbital reduces duvelisib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 43. Edoxaban: Phenobarbital reduces edoxaban levels via P-glycoprotein efflux. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 44. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 46. Elagolix: Phenobarbital reduces elagolix levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 47. Elbasvir/Grazoprevir: Phenobarbital reduces the efficacy of this combination therapy via CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 48. Eletiptan: Phenobarbital reduces eletiptan levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 49. Eliglustat: Phenobarbital reduces eliglustat levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 50. Elranatamab: Elranatamab may increase phenobarbital levels by suppressing CYP enzyme activity. Monitor closely. 51. Eltrombopag: Phenobarbital reduces eltrombopag levels via CYP1A2 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Monitor closely. 52. Ethosuximide: Phenobarbital reduces ethosuximide levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 74. Ethotoin: Phenobarbital reduces ethotoin levels via CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Monitor closely. 75. Etoposide: Phenobarbital reduces etoposide levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 78. Etravirine: Phenobarbital reduces etravirine levels via CYP3A4, CYP2C19, and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated.
